messages.content: Help me validate that the caller-sensitive method has correctly injected an invoker class for the `CSM` instance `csmInstance` and that the expected class is `MyExpectedClass.class` in a unit test?

function.name: MethodInvokeTest_checkInjectedInvoker
function.description: Checks if the injected invoker class in the CSM instance is hidden, belongs to the same module as the expected class, and appears before the expected class on the stack. Note that the provided function is in Java 8 SDK syntax.

csm.description: The CSM instance to check for the injected invoker. This parameter can be of any type of Java object in string representation.

expected.description: The expected class to compare against the injected invoker. This parameter can be of any type of Java object in string representation.

message.reasoning: The user wants to validate that the caller-sensitive method has correctly injected an invoker class for the CSM instance csmInstance and that the expected class is MyExpectedClass.class in a unit test. We have a tool that checks if the injected invoker class in the CSM instance is hidden, belongs to the same module as the expected class, and appears before the expected class on the stack. The tool expects a JSON with csm and expected. The user didn't provide the actual values for csm or expected. They said csmInstance and MyExpectedClass.class. We can pass those as strings. The tool expects the csm instance to be a string representation of a Java object. We can pass "csmInstance" as the string representation. The expected class is "MyExpectedClass.class". So we can call the tool with csm: "csmInstance" and expected: "MyExpectedClass.class".
